title: Capacity: Litres and Centilitres
seo_title: Capacity – Primary 4 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Identify standard containers; measure capacity in litres and centilitres; add, subtract, multiply and divide capacities; solve real-life problems. (summary of the NERDC Primary 4 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 4 maths worksheets on capacity: litres and centilitres, adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing capacities, reading containers and estimating. 100 questions with answers.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Capacity is how much a container can hold. We measure it in litres and centilitres (cl): 1 litre = 100 cl.
  • Change to centilitres to calculate: 2 litres 35 cl = 235 cl.
  • Standard containers include 50 cl bottles, 1-litre bottles, 25-litre jerrycans and 200-litre drums.

Examples

Example

3 litres 60 cl + 1 litre 75 cl

360 cl + 175 cl = 535 cl

Answer: 5 litres 35 cl

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
1 litre = 1,000 cl1 litre = 100 cl (1,000 ml).
Adding litres and cl without regrouping135 cl = 1 litre 35 cl.
Reading the wrong markFind what each small mark is worth.
